# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# cargo_deny - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cargo-deny

## Expand description

See the [book 📕](https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/) for in-depth documentation.

To run on CI as a GitHub Action, see [ cargo-deny-action](https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action).

*Please Note: This is a tool that we use (and like!) and it makes sense to us to release it as open source. However, we can’t take any responsibility for your use of the tool, if it will function correctly or fulfil your needs. No functionality in - or information provided by - cargo-deny constitutes legal advice.*

`cargo install --locked cargo-deny && cargo deny init && cargo deny check`[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

If you want to use `cargo-deny` without having `cargo` installed, build `cargo-deny` with the `standalone` feature. This can be useful in Docker Images.

```
cargo install --locked cargo-deny
# Or, if you're an Arch user
pacman -S cargo-deny
```
[§](https://docs.rs#initialize-your-project)[Initialize](https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/cli/init.html) your project

`cargo deny init``cargo deny check`The licenses check is used to verify that every crate you use has license terms you find acceptable.

`cargo deny check licenses`The bans check is used to deny (or allow) specific crates, as well as detect and handle multiple versions of the same crate.

`cargo deny check bans`The advisories check is used to detect issues for crates by looking in an advisory database.

`cargo deny check advisories`The sources check ensures crates only come from sources you trust.

`cargo deny check sources`[§](https://docs.rs#pre-commit-hook)Pre-commit hook

You can use `cargo-deny` with [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com). Add it to your local `.pre-commit-config.yaml` as follows:

```
- repo: https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny
  rev: 0.14.16 # choose your preferred tag
  hooks:
    - id: cargo-deny
      args: ["--all-features", "check"] # optionally modify the arguments for cargo-deny (default arguments shown here)
```

# Deserialize in serde::de - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde/latest/serde/de/trait.Deserialize.html

`pub trait Deserialize<'de>: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
    // Required method
    fn [deserialize](https://docs.rs#tymethod.deserialize)<D>(deserializer: D) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, D::[Error](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html#associatedtype.Error)>
       where D: [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)<'de>;
}## Expand description

A **data structure** that can be deserialized from any data format supported
by Serde.

Serde provides `Deserialize` implementations for many Rust primitive and
standard library types. The complete list is [here](https://docs.rs/index.html). All of these
can be deserialized using Serde out of the box.

Additionally, Serde provides a procedural macro called `serde_derive` to
automatically generate `Deserialize` implementations for structs and enums
in your program. See the [derive section of the manual](https://serde.rs/derive.html) for how to
use this.

In rare cases it may be necessary to implement `Deserialize` manually for
some type in your program. See the [Implementing
 Deserialize](https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html) section of the manual for more about this.

Third-party crates may provide `Deserialize` implementations for types that
they expose. For example the `linked-hash-map` crate provides a
`LinkedHashMap<K, V>` type that is deserializable by Serde because the crate
provides an implementation of `Deserialize` for it.

[§](https://docs.rs#lifetime)Lifetime

The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
borrowed by `Self` when deserialized. See the page [Understanding
deserializer lifetimes](https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html) for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# pivx_rpc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pivx-rpc/0.4.0/pivx_rpc/

## Expand description

PIVX SDK: typed JSON-RPC client for pivxd with first-class support for shielded (SHIELD/Sapling) balances and transactions.

```
use pivx_rpc::{Auth, PivxClient, ShieldRecipient, ShieldWatcher, WatchOptions};
let client = PivxClient::new(
    "http://127.0.0.1:51473",
    Auth::UserPass { user: "rpcuser".into(), pass: "rpcpass".into() },
)?;
// Watch a shielded address via its viewing key (no spend key needed).
let imported = client.import_sapling_viewing_key("p-view-key...", None, None).await?;
let mut watcher = ShieldWatcher::new(&client, WatchOptions {
    addresses: vec![imported.address],
    ..Default::default()
});
let events = watcher.poll().await?; // first poll primes silently
// Send shielded funds (node wallet holds the keys and builds the proof).
let txid = client
    .shield_send_many(
        pivx_rpc::FromAddress::AnyShield,
        &[ShieldRecipient::new("ps1...", 1.5).with_memo("hello")],
    )
    .await?;
```

# sim_lib_pitch_namer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-pitch-namer/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_pitch_namer/

## Expand description

Multi-school cluster naming for the SIM music libraries.

This crate is the aggregator over the pitch-naming schools. It defines the
shared [ ClusterNamer](https://docs.rs/trait.ClusterNamer.html) trait and the

[taxonomy, then drives every built-in school – Forte set-class names, functional roman numerals, plain set-theory prime forms, neo-Riemannian labels, and jazz chord symbols – through one](https://docs.rs/enum.NamingSchool.html)

`NamingSchool`[. The registry can label a pitch-class set in every school at once and translate a label from one school to another. The schools themselves live in the](https://docs.rs/struct.NamerRegistry.html)

`NamerRegistry``sim-lib-pitch-namer-*` sibling crates; this
crate composes them and exposes them as a SIM runtime library through
[/](https://docs.rs/struct.PitchNamerLib.html)

`PitchNamerLib`[.](https://docs.rs/fn.install_pitch_namer_lib.html)

`install_pitch_namer_lib`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cluster](https://docs.rs/struct.ClusterLabel.html)- Label
- A label produced by one naming school for one pitch-class set.
- [Cluster](https://docs.rs/struct.ClusterMeta.html)- Meta
- Metadata attached to a produced `ClusterLabel`
- [Label](https://docs.rs/struct.LabelContext.html)- Context
- The context a namer may use: an optional chord root and an optional key.
- [Namer](https://docs.rs/struct.NamerRegistry.html)- Registry
- A registry of `ClusterNamer`
- [Pitch](https://docs.rs/struct.PitchNamerLib.html)- Namer - Lib
- Host-registered lib exporting the built-in cluster-namer cards and registry,
built on the shared `SurfacePackLib`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Naming](https://docs.rs/enum.NamingSchool.html)- School
- A school of chord and pitch-set naming.
- [Pitch](https://docs.rs/enum.PitchNamerError.html)- Namer - Error
- Error returned by naming-registry operations.

# facett - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett/0.1.10/facett/

## Expand description

**facett** — umbrella crate. One dependency that re-exports every component,
so a consumer writes `facett::graph::GraphView` / `facett::map::MapView` etc.
instead of pulling each `facett-*` crate. The `Facet` model + the headless

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [clip](https://docs.rs/clip/index.html)
- **Cross-facet typed copy/paste**(§16) — the trait + payload machinery so copy/paste carries- **full typed data**between facett components, not just text. A process-wide transfer registry holds the last typed- `ClipPayload`
- [effects](https://docs.rs/effects/index.html)
- **effects**— motion + bloom for the facett look. Pure egui,- **glow backend only**: everything here paints with layered alpha shapes on an- `egui::Painter`
- [harness](https://docs.rs/harness/index.html)
- Headless test harness — **fire up a**: its`Facet`, inject data, render it offscreen, and capture what it drew`state_json`+ a vertex count (a “it drew something” proxy) + a stderr activity trail. No display, no GPU. This is the basis of facett’s auto test matrix, and mirrors nornir viz’s`NORNIR_VIZ_STATE`introspection — every component is observable from outside.
- [look](https://docs.rs/look/index.html)
- **facett look & feel**(the work-order architecture, §3) — one- `Theme`- **Windows**,- **macOS**,- **Device**(effects-off, rugged/military). The- `Theme`- *single source of truth*:- `Theme::apply`- `egui::Style`(visuals + spacing + scroll) plus the text scale in one call, and also publishes the derived legacy- `crate::Theme`
- [nav](https://docs.rs/nav/index.html)
- **Shared spatial navigation + focus**(§13 FOC-2, §14 NAV-1) — the- *one*pan/zoom model (- `Navigable`) reused by map/graph/plot/canvas, and the- *one*spatial focus rule (- `nearest_in_direction`) reused by pane and form navigation (COH-3). Pan/zoom is expressed as an- `egui::emath::TSTransform`(scale + offset), so a host can also use it to transform an overlaid guest layer (§5 CMP-4).
- [scroll_](https://docs.rs/scroll_engine/index.html)- engine
- **CygnusEd smooth-scroll engine**(§11) — pixel-by-pixel, sub-pixel soft scrolling with momentum/acceleration, à la the Amiga editor’s jerkyless feel. The scroll- *offset*is decoupled from row height (renderers paint at a- **fractional**pixel offset + clip), and the whole thing is- **deterministic under an injected clock**(- `advance(dt)`), so snapshots reproduce exactly (FC-7 / P0-5). Reusable by text, console, and the dataframe grid (SCRL-3).
- [theme](https://docs.rs/theme/index.html)
- **Theming.**A palette the custom-painted components (graph/depgraph/map) read from the egui context, plus matching egui- `Visuals`for the standard widgets (pop/table/pipeline). Call- `set_theme`- `Theme::default`- `Theme::sci_fi`- `Theme::nordic_aurora`- `Theme::cyberpunk_neon`- `Theme::amber_crt`- `Theme::deep_space`- `Theme::hugin_noir`- `Theme::ALL`- `Theme::by_name`

# facett_map3d_flight - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-map3d-flight/0.1.10/facett_map3d_flight/

## Expand description

**facett-map3d-flight** — the AAA planetary **FLIGHT-SIM** engine layer over the
lightweight, embeddable [ facett_map3d](https://docs.rs/facett-map3d/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_map3d/index.html) map. This crate carries the heavy,
GPU-required, full-screen “bells and whistles”;

`facett-map3d` stays lean
(flat ground + extruded house markers, CPU-fallback, deck-pane-embeddable).[§](https://docs.rs#what-has-landed-here-cpu-foundation--build--test-green-headless)What has LANDED here (CPU foundation — build + test green, headless)

- `origin`- **floating origin**: an- `f64`Web-Mercator world frame + per-frame camera-centred rebase to- `f32`, killing far-from-origin vertex jitter / Z-fighting at planetary scale (FLIGHT-SIM #1).
- `atmos`- **precomputed atmospheric scattering**: a Bruneton/Hillaire-style transmittance LUT + single-scatter sky-view + aerial perspective, feeding both the sky AND the terrain/building haze, varying with altitude + sun angle (FLIGHT-SIM #2). Derived sky tints are ready to drive- `facett_map3d`’s existing analytic- `sky.wgsl`uniforms.
- `camera_fly`- **camera rig**: a deterministic 6DOF state machine (free-fly primary / cinematic orbit / flight-stick) over the- `f64`world frame, exercising the floating origin.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-is-roadmapped--spiked-see-nornirflightsim-engine-roadmapmd)What is ROADMAPPED / spiked (see `.nornir/flightsim-engine-roadmap.md`)

GPU scattering-LUT precompute pass, GPU-compute building extrusion (BuildingMeta
marshaller + indirect draw), CDLOD/quadtree DEM terrain + the drape fix, and the
out-of-core Hilbert-sorted GeoParquet streaming. The shared `Mesh3` + wgpu
pipeline + sky/water shaders are **reused** from `facett_map3d` (re-exported
below), not forked.

Everything that lands here is pure CPU math (no GPU, no egui at the foundation layer), so the precision + scattering + rig invariants are directly inject-assert-testable and deterministic (FC-7).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [camera_](https://docs.rs/camera_fly/index.html)- fly

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Mesh3](https://docs.rs/struct.Mesh3.html)
- Re-export the shared, reused pieces from the lightweight map so flight-sim
callers extend (not fork) them: the extruded mesh contract + the sun/sky model
(the seam the scattering plugs into) + the LOD ladder.
A 3D mesh of the extruded map: positions + per-vertex normals (parallel) +
per-**triangle**source colours + triangle indices. Coordinates are in the normalised`[-1, 1]`design box (x right,**y up**, z depth) with the ground at`y = 0`and prisms rising to`+height`.
- [SunSky](https://docs.rs/struct.SunSky.html)
- Re-export the shared, reused pieces from the lightweight map so flight-sim
callers extend (not fork) them: the extruded mesh contract + the sun/sky model
(the seam the scattering plugs into) + the LOD ladder.
A directional sun + sky environment. All colours are linear-ish `[r,g,b]`in`0..1`;`dir`points FROM the surface TO the sun (the convention the PBR shader’s`dot(n, l)`wants).

# xcelerator_solver - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xcelerator-solver/0.1.0/xcelerator_solver/

## Expand description

Xcelerator Solver — deterministic, precision-configurable symbolic regression engine.

Given tabular data (CSV) and an explicit vocabulary of allowed terms and operators, the solver exhaustively searches for mathematical expressions that explain the data within a user-specified error threshold.

[§](https://docs.rs#design-principles)Design principles

- **Deterministic**— Bottom-Up Enumeration (BUE) always finds the simplest formula at any error level first. Identical inputs produce identical results.
- **Explicit pool**— only declared terms and operators are used; no hidden defaults, no open-ended constant optimization.
- **Configurable precision**— expressions can be evaluated at arbitrary MPFR precision (- `--features hp`); named constants (- `Pi`,- `e`,- `gamma`, …) are materialized at full target precision via MPFR built-ins.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start-library-usage)Quick start (library usage)

```
use xcelerator_solver::{SolverConfig, solve};
let config = SolverConfig::load("solver.toml".as_ref()).unwrap();
let result = solve(config).unwrap();
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use config::`- [SolverConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.SolverConfig.html);
- `pub use output::`- [FinalEntry](https://docs.rs/output/struct.FinalEntry.html);
- `pub use output::`- [run_validation](https://docs.rs/output/fn.run_validation.html);
- `pub use output::`- [print_table](https://docs.rs/output/fn.print_table.html);
- `pub use output::`- [print_json](https://docs.rs/output/fn.print_json.html);
- `pub use output::`- [Tee](https://docs.rs/output/struct.Tee.html);
- `pub use pipeline::`- [PipelineResult](https://docs.rs/pipeline/struct.PipelineResult.html);
- `pub use pipeline::`- [SearchStats](https://docs.rs/pipeline/struct.SearchStats.html);
- `pub use pipeline::`- [run_pipeline](https://docs.rs/pipeline/fn.run_pipeline.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [aggregator](https://docs.rs/aggregator/index.html)
- Aggregator: bounded top-X heap, error-threshold filter, pinned check.
- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- TOML configuration loading and validation for the solver.
- [csv_](https://docs.rs/csv_loader/index.html)- loader
- CSV parsing into DataPoints (f64 and HP variants).
- [error_](https://docs.rs/error_metric/index.html)- metric
- MAPE, MAE, and RMSE error metrics — f64 and HP variants.
- [eval](https://docs.rs/eval/index.html)
- f64 expression evaluator.
- [evaluator](https://docs.rs/evaluator/index.html)
- Evaluator worker pool.
- [expr](https://docs.rs/expr/index.html)
- Expression AST: types, canonical form, display, subtree containment.
- [generator](https://docs.rs/generator/index.html)
- Streaming candidate generator — two-level parallel design.
- [output](https://docs.rs/output/index.html)
- Output module: validation scoring, table/JSON formatting, Tee writer.
- [pinned](https://docs.rs/pinned/index.html)
- Pinned sub-components: expression string parser and containment check.
- [pipeline](https://docs.rs/pipeline/index.html)
- Pipeline wiring: owns VisitedSet, spawns threads, connects all actors.
- [vocabulary](https://docs.rs/vocabulary/index.html)
- Vocabulary: allowed terms, operators, constants, and seed expressions. Maps spelled-out config names (“add”, “multiply”, “Pi”) to typed values.

- Run the solver end-to-end.

# mongreldb_kit - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mongreldb-kit/0.9.0/mongreldb_kit/

## Expand description

Storage-backed MongrelDB Kit crate.

This crate wraps MongrelDB core with the kit schema model, transaction semantics, query execution, and migration runner.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use db::`- [ApproxAggKind](https://docs.rs/db/enum.ApproxAggKind.html);
- `pub use db::`- [ApproxAggregate](https://docs.rs/db/struct.ApproxAggregate.html);
- `pub use db::`- [Database](https://docs.rs/db/struct.Database.html);
- `pub use db::`- [ExplainPlan](https://docs.rs/db/struct.ExplainPlan.html);
- `pub use db::`- [IncrementalAggKind](https://docs.rs/db/enum.IncrementalAggKind.html);
- `pub use db::`- [IncrementalAggregate](https://docs.rs/db/struct.IncrementalAggregate.html);
- `pub use db::`- [SimilarRow](https://docs.rs/db/struct.SimilarRow.html);
- `pub use error::`- [KitError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.KitError.html);
- `pub use error::`- [Result](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html);
- `pub use migrate::`- [migrate](https://docs.rs/migrate/fn.migrate.html);
- `pub use query::`- [JoinRow](https://docs.rs/query/type.JoinRow.html);
- `pub use schema::`- [Row](https://docs.rs/schema/struct.Row.html);
- `pub use txn::`- [Transaction](https://docs.rs/txn/struct.Transaction.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [check](https://docs.rs/check/index.html)
- Evaluation of table/column check constraints.
- [db](https://docs.rs/db/index.html)
- Database handle for `mongreldb-kit`.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error model for `mongreldb-kit`.
- [keys](https://docs.rs/keys/index.html)
- Key encoding for Kit indexes, guards, and primary keys.
- [migrate](https://docs.rs/migrate/index.html)
- Migration runner for `mongreldb-kit`.
- [migrations](https://docs.rs/migrations/index.html)
- Migration planning and checksums.
- [planner](https://docs.rs/planner/index.html)
- Delete planning: compute the set of rows affected by a delete, including cascade, set-null, and restrict foreign-key actions.
- [procedure](https://docs.rs/procedure/index.html)
- [pushdown](https://docs.rs/pushdown/index.html)
- Predicate pushdown: translate Kit `Expr`predicates into MongrelDB core`Condition`s so the native engine can resolve them via indexes instead of a full-scan + Rust evaluation (Kit Priority 1).
- [query](https://docs.rs/query/index.html)
- Query execution for kit statements.
- [schema](https://docs.rs/schema/index.html)
- Schema/value conversion between the kit model and MongrelDB core.
- [tsv](https://docs.rs/tsv/index.html)
- TSV import/export for kit tables.
- [txn](https://docs.rs/txn/index.html)
- Kit transaction wrapper around a MongrelDB core transaction.
- [validation](https://docs.rs/validation/index.html)
- Row validation against a `Table`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Aggregate](https://docs.rs/struct.Aggregate.html)

- [Aggregate](https://docs.rs/struct.AggregateQuery.html)- Query
- A grouped/aggregated query. Rows are scanned, optionally filtered, grouped by
`group_by`key columns, reduced with`aggregates`, and finally filtered by`having`. With no`group_by`, the whole (filtered) table is one group.

- A nested-loop join query. The result is a list of combined rows; each combined
row is a JSON object keyed by table alias whose values are that source’s row
object (or JSON `null`for an unmatched right side of a`LEFT`join). Column references in`filter`/`order_by`/join`on`must be qualified (`alias.column`).

# ggen_a2a_mcp - Rust

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ggen-a2a-mcp---agent-to-agent-protocol-and-mcp-server)ggen-a2a-mcp - Agent-to-Agent Protocol and MCP Server

A2A protocol implementation for agent-to-agent communication with Model Context Protocol (MCP) server support.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Artifact and artifact collection types

- Health monitoring and status tracking

# mongreldb_kit_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mongreldb-kit-core/0.9.0/mongreldb_kit_core/

## Expand description

Core, language-neutral model for MongrelDB Kit.

This crate contains the schema model, key encoding, validation, constraint
planning, migration planning, and query AST used by the storage-backed
`mongreldb-kit` crate and by language bindings.

# cargo_deny - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cargo-deny/0.19.9/target-redirect/cargo_deny/

## Expand description

See the [book 📕](https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/) for in-depth documentation.

To run on CI as a GitHub Action, see [ cargo-deny-action](https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action).

*Please Note: This is a tool that we use (and like!) and it makes sense to us to release it as open source. However, we can’t take any responsibility for your use of the tool, if it will function correctly or fulfil your needs. No functionality in - or information provided by - cargo-deny constitutes legal advice.*

`cargo install --locked cargo-deny && cargo deny init && cargo deny check`[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

If you want to use `cargo-deny` without having `cargo` installed, build `cargo-deny` with the `standalone` feature. This can be useful in Docker Images.

```
cargo install --locked cargo-deny
# Or, if you're an Arch user
pacman -S cargo-deny
```
[§](https://docs.rs#initialize-your-project)[Initialize](https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/cli/init.html) your project

`cargo deny init``cargo deny check`The licenses check is used to verify that every crate you use has license terms you find acceptable.

`cargo deny check licenses`The bans check is used to deny (or allow) specific crates, as well as detect and handle multiple versions of the same crate.

`cargo deny check bans`The advisories check is used to detect issues for crates by looking in an advisory database.

`cargo deny check advisories`The sources check ensures crates only come from sources you trust.

`cargo deny check sources`[§](https://docs.rs#pre-commit-hook)Pre-commit hook

You can use `cargo-deny` with [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com). Add it to your local `.pre-commit-config.yaml` as follows:

```
- repo: https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny
  rev: 0.14.16 # choose your preferred tag
  hooks:
    - id: cargo-deny
      args: ["--all-features", "check"] # optionally modify the arguments for cargo-deny (default arguments shown here)
```

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckCtx.html)- Ctx
- Common context for the various checks. Some checks require additional information though.

- Error that can occur when deserializing TOML.
- [Kid](https://docs.rs/struct.Kid.html)
- A crate’s unique identifier
- [Krate](https://docs.rs/struct.Krate.html)
- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html)
- A slice of a UTF-8 path (akin to `str`
- [PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html)
- An owned, mutable UTF-8 path (akin to `String`
- [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)
- A start and end location within a toml document
- [Spanned](https://docs.rs/struct.Spanned.html)
- An arbitrary `T`with additional span information
- [Version](https://docs.rs/struct.Version.html)
- **SemVer version**as defined by- [https://semver.org](https://semver.org).

- [DepKind](https://docs.rs/enum.DepKind.html)

- The possible lint levels for the various lints. These function similarly
to the standard [Rust lint levels](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/lints/levels.html)

- [Source](https://docs.rs/enum.Source.html)

[485](#485)#[inline]
[492](#492)pub(crate) fn normalize_git_url(url: &mut Url) -> (GitSpec, Option<String>) {
[493](#493)    const GIT_EXT: &str = ".git";
[494](#494)
[495](#495)    let needs_chopping = url.path().ends_with(&GIT_EXT);
[496](#496)    if needs_chopping {
[497](#497)        let last = {
[498](#498)            let last = url.path_segments().unwrap().next_back().unwrap();
[499](#499)            last[..last.len() - GIT_EXT.len()].to_owned()
[500](#500)        };
[501](#501)        url.path_segments_mut().unwrap().pop().push(&last);
[502](#502)    }
[503](#503)
[504](#504)    if url.path().ends_with('/') {
[505](#505)        url.path_segments_mut().unwrap().pop_if_empty();
[506](#506)    }
[507](#507)
[508](#508)    let mut spec = GitSpec::Any;
[509](#509)    let mut spec_value = None;
[510](#510)
[511](#511)    for (k, v) in url.query_pairs() {
[512](#512)        spec = match k.as_ref() {
[513](#513)            "branch" | "ref" => GitSpec::Branch,
[514](#514)            "tag" => GitSpec::Tag,
[515](#515)            "rev" => GitSpec::Rev,
[516](#516)            _ => continue,
[517](#517)        };
[518](#518)
[519](#519)        spec_value = Some(v.into_owned());
[520](#520)    }
[521](#521)
[522](#522)    if url
[523](#523)        .query_pairs()
[524](#524)        .any(|(k, v)| k == "branch" && v == "master")
[525](#525)    {
[526](#526)        if url.query_pairs().count() == 1 {
[527](#527)            url.set_query(None);
[528](#528)        } else {
[529](#529)            let mut nq = String::new();
[530](#530)            for (k, v) in url.query_pairs() {
[531](#531)                if k == "branch" && v == "master" {
[532](#532)                    continue;
[533](#533)                }
[534](#534)
[535](#535)                use std::fmt::Write;
[536](#536)                write!(&mut nq, "{k}={v}&").unwrap();
[537](#537)            }
[538](#538)
[539](#539)            nq.pop();
[541](#541)            url.set_query(Some(&nq));
[542](#542)        }
[543](#543)    }
[544](#544)
[545](#545)    (spec, spec_value)
[546](#546)}

[565](#565)        .context("unable to determine crates.io url")?;

[569](#569)    )

[572](#572)    let lock = tame_index::utils::flock::FileLock::unlocked();

[578](#578)        let mut cache = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
[579](#579)        for name in krates {
[580](#580)            let read = || -> Option<krates::index::IndexKrate> {
[581](#581)                let name = name.as_str().try_into().ok()?;
[582](#582)                let krate = index.cached_krate(name, &lock).ok()??;
[583](#583)                let versions = krate
[584](#584)                    .versions

[586](#586)                    .filter_map(|kv| {
[587](#587)                        kv.version.parse::<semver::Version>().ok().map(|version| {
[591](#591)                            krates::index::IndexKrateVersion {
[592](#592)                                version,

[594](#594)                                    .features()

[597](#597)                            }

[599](#599)                    })
[600](#600)                    .collect();
[601](#601)
[602](#602)                Some(krates::index::IndexKrate { versions })
[603](#603)            };
[604](#604)
[605](#605)            let krate = read();
[606](#606)            cache.insert(name, krate);
[607](#607)        }
[608](#608)
[609](#609)        cache
[610](#610)    };

# cargo_deny::licenses - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cargo-deny/0.19.9/cargo_deny/licenses/index.html

## Expand description

Configuration and logic for checking crate licenses

[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-deny-check-licenses)`cargo deny check licenses`

One important aspect that one must always keep in mind when using code from
other people is what the licensing of that code is and whether it fits the
requirements of your project. Luckily, most of the crates in the Rust
ecosystem tend to follow the example set forth by Rust itself, namely
dual-license `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, but of course, that is not always the case.

`cargo-deny` allows you to ensure that all of your dependencies have license
requirements that are satisfied by the licenses you choose to use for your
project, and notifies you via warnings or errors if the license requirements
for any crate aren’t compatible with your configuration.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [cfg](https://docs.rs/cfg/index.html)
- Configuration for license checking

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Gatherer](https://docs.rs/struct.Gatherer.html)
- [License](https://docs.rs/struct.LicenseStore.html)- Store
- Store used to identify licenses from text files
- [Summary](https://docs.rs/struct.Summary.html)

# Path in cargo_deny - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cargo-deny/0.19.9/cargo_deny/struct.Path.html

`pub struct Path(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A slice of a UTF-8 path (akin to [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)).

This type supports a number of operations for inspecting a path, including
breaking the path into its components (separated by `/` on Unix and by either
`/` or `\` on Windows), extracting the file name, determining whether the path
is absolute, and so on.

This is an *unsized* type, meaning that it must always be used behind a
pointer like `&` or [ Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html). For an owned version of this type,
see

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
// Note: this example does work on Windows
let path = Utf8Path::new("./foo/bar.txt");
let parent = path.parent();
assert_eq!(parent, Some(Utf8Path::new("./foo")));
let file_stem = path.file_stem();
assert_eq!(file_stem, Some("bar"));
let extension = path.extension();
assert_eq!(extension, Some("txt"));
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Directly wraps a string slice as a [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html) slice.

This is a cost-free conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
Utf8Path::new("foo.txt");
```
You can create [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html)s from

[s, or even other](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`String`[s:](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html)

`Utf8Path````
use camino::Utf8Path;
let string = String::from("foo.txt");
let from_string = Utf8Path::new(&string);
let from_path = Utf8Path::new(&from_string);
assert_eq!(from_string, from_path);
```
Converts a [ Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html) to a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html)

`Utf8Path`Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path is not valid UTF-8.

For a version that returns a type that implements [ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/error/trait.Error.html),
see

[.](https://docs.rs#impl-TryFrom%3C%26Path%3E-for-%26Utf8Path)

`TryFrom<&Path>`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let unicode_path = Path::new("/valid/unicode");
Utf8Path::from_path(unicode_path).expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
let non_unicode_path = Path::new(non_unicode_str);
assert!(Utf8Path::from_path(non_unicode_path).is_none(), "non-Unicode path failed");
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#854)#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#854)

#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html) is absolute, i.e., if it is independent of
the current directory.

-
On Unix, a path is absolute if it starts with the root, so `is_absolute`and`has_root`
-
On Windows, a path is absolute if it has a prefix and starts with the root: `C:\windows`is absolute, while`C:temp`and`\temp`are not.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("foo.txt").is_absolute());
```
Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html) has a root.

-
On Unix, a path has a root if it begins with `/`.
-
On Windows, a path has a root if it: - has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g., `\windows`
- has a prefix followed by a separator, e.g., `C:\windows`but not`C:windows`
- has any non-disk prefix, e.g., `\\server\share`

- has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g.,

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/etc/passwd").has_root());
```
Returns the [ Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html) without its final component, if there is one.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in a root or prefix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-11)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar");
let parent = path.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(parent, Utf8Path::new("/foo"));
let grand_parent = parent.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(grand_parent, Utf8Path::new("/"));
assert_eq!(grand_parent.parent(), None);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#954)

#### pub fn [ancestors](https://docs.rs#method.ancestors)(&self) -> [Utf8Ancestors](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/camino/struct.Utf8Ancestors.html)<'_>

Produces an iterator over [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html) and its ancestors.

The iterator will yield the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html) that is returned if the

[method is used zero or more times. That means, the iterator will yield](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.parent)

`parent``&self`, `&self.parent().unwrap()`,
`&self.parent().unwrap().parent().unwrap()` and so on. If the [method returns](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.parent)

`parent`[, the iterator will do likewise. The iterator will always yield at least one value, namely](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None``&self`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-12)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar").ancestors();
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar").ancestors();
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("..")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
```
Returns the final component of the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html), if there is one.

If the path is a normal file, this is the file name. If it’s the path of a directory, this is the directory name.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in

`..`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-13)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert_eq!(Some("bin"), Utf8Path::new("/usr/bin/").file_name());
assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("tmp/foo.txt").file_name());
assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/.").file_name());
assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/.//").file_name());
assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/..").file_name());
assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("/").file_name());
```

Determines whether `base` is a prefix of `self`.

Only considers whole path components to match.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/etc/passwd");
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc"));
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc/"));
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc/passwd"));
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc/passwd/")); // extra slash is okay
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc/passwd///")); // multiple extra slashes are okay
assert!(!path.starts_with("/e"));
assert!(!path.starts_with("/etc/passwd.txt"));
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("/etc/foo.rs").starts_with("/etc/foo"));
```
Determines whether `child` is a suffix of `self`.

Only considers whole path components to match.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-16)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/etc/resolv.conf");
assert!(path.ends_with("resolv.conf"));
assert!(path.ends_with("etc/resolv.conf"));
assert!(path.ends_with("/etc/resolv.conf"));
assert!(!path.ends_with("/resolv.conf"));
assert!(!path.ends_with("conf")); // use .extension() instead
```
Extracts the stem (non-extension) portion of [ self.file_name](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.file_name).

The stem is:

- `None`
- The entire file name if there is no embedded `.`;
- The entire file name if the file name begins with `.`and has no other`.`s within;
- Otherwise, the portion of the file name before the final `.`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-17)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert_eq!("foo", Utf8Path::new("foo.rs").file_stem().unwrap());

Extracts the prefix of [ self.file_name](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.file_name).

The prefix is:

- `None`
- The entire file name if there is no embedded `.`;
- The portion of the file name before the first non-beginning `.`;
- The entire file name if the file name begins with `.`and has no other`.`s within;
- The portion of the file name before the second `.`if the file name begins with`.`

```

- `None`

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300)#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/camino/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300)

#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/camino/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_>

Produces an iterator over the [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/camino/enum.Utf8Component.html)s of the path.

When parsing the path, there is a small amount of normalization:

-
Repeated separators are ignored, so `a/b`and`a//b`both have`a`and`b`as components.
-
Occurrences of `.`are normalized away, except if they are at the beginning of the path. For example,`a/./b`,`a/b/`,`a/b/.`and`a/b`all have`a`and`b`as components, but`./a/b`starts with an additional`CurDir`
-
A trailing slash is normalized away, `/a/b`and`/a/b/`are equivalent.

Note that no other normalization takes place; in particular, `a/c`
and `a/b/../c` are distinct, to account for the possibility that `b`
is a symbolic link (so its parent isn’t `a`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-25)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
let mut components = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").components();
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::RootDir));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("tmp")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), None)
```
Produces an iterator over the path’s components viewed as [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)
slices.

For more information about the particulars of how the path is separated
into components, see [ components](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.components).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-26)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut it = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").iter();
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string().as_str()));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("tmp"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("foo.txt"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), None)
```

Returns `true` if the path points at an existing entity.

Warning: this method may be error-prone, consider using [ try_exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.try_exists) instead!
It also has a risk of introducing time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt").exists());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581)#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)>

#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)>

Returns `Ok(true)` if the path points at an existing entity.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `Ok(false)`.

As opposed to the [ exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.exists) method, this one doesn’t silently ignore errors
unrelated to the path not existing. (E.g. it will return

[in case of permission denied on some of the parent directories.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)

`Err`Note that while this avoids some pitfalls of the `exists()` method, it still can not
prevent time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs. You should only use it in scenarios
where those bugs are not an issue.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(
    !Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt")
        .try_exists()
        .expect("Can't check existence of file does_not_exist.txt")
);
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/root/secret_file.txt").try_exists().is_err());
```
Returns `true` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a regular file.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-37)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;

[. Then call](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)

`Result`[if it was](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.Metadata.html#method.is_file)

`fs::Metadata::is_file`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)

`Ok`When the goal is simply to read from (or write to) the source, the most
reliable way to test the source can be read (or written to) is to open
it. Only using `is_file` can break workflows like `diff <( prog_a )` on
a Unix-like system for example. See [ fs::File::open](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.File.html#method.open) or

[for more information.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.OpenOptions.html#method.open)

`fs::OpenOptions::open`Returns `true` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a directory.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-38)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("./is_a_directory/").is_dir(), true);
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("a_file.txt").is_dir(), false);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also-2)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
check errors, call [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html) and handle its

[. Then call](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)

`Result`[if it was](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.Metadata.html#method.is_dir)

`fs::Metadata::is_dir`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)

`Ok`Returns `true` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a symbolic link.

This function will not traverse symbolic links. In case of a broken symbolic link this will also return true.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a permission error, this will return false.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-39)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::os::unix::fs::symlink;
let link_path = Utf8Path::new("link");
symlink("/origin_does_not_exist/", link_path).unwrap();
assert_eq!(link_path.is_symlink(), true);
assert_eq!(link_path.exists(), false);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also-3)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
check errors, call [ Utf8Path::symlink_metadata](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.symlink_metadata) and handle its

[. Then call](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)

`Result`[if it was](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.Metadata.html#method.is_symlink)

`fs::Metadata::is_symlink`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)

Returns the original [ OsStr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/ffi/os_str/struct.OsStr.html) if it is not valid UTF-8.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-40)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::convert::TryFrom;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
assert!(<&Utf8Path>::try_from(non_unicode_str).is_err(), "non-Unicode string path failed");
```
Returns [ FromPathError](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/camino/struct.FromPathError.html) if the path is not valid UTF-8.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-41)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::convert::TryFrom;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let unicode_path = Path::new("/valid/unicode");
<&Utf8Path>::try_from(unicode_path).expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
let non_unicode_path = Path::new(non_unicode_str);
assert!(<&Utf8Path>::try_from(non_unicode_path).is_err(), "non-Unicode path failed");
```

# PathBuf in cargo_deny - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cargo-deny/0.19.9/cargo_deny/struct.PathBuf.html

`pub struct PathBuf(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

An owned, mutable UTF-8 path (akin to [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)).

This type provides methods like [ push](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html#method.push) and

[that mutate the path in place. It also implements](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html#method.set_extension)

`set_extension`[to](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/deref/trait.Deref.html)

`Deref`[, meaning that all methods on](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[slices are available on](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[values as well.](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

You can use [ push](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html#method.push) to build up a

[from components:](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf````
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::new();
path.push(r"C:\");
path.push("windows");
path.push("system32");
path.set_extension("dll");
```
However, [ push](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html#method.push) is best used for dynamic situations. This is a better way
to do this when you know all of the components ahead of time:

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let path: Utf8PathBuf = [r"C:\", "windows", "system32.dll"].iter().collect();
```
We can still do better than this! Since these are all strings, we can use
[ From::from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html#tymethod.from):

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let path = Utf8PathBuf::from(r"C:\windows\system32.dll");
```
Which method works best depends on what kind of situation you’re in.

Converts a [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html) to a

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)

`PathBuf`This is equivalent to the [ From<Utf8PathBuf> for PathBuf](https://docs.rs#impl-From%3CUtf8PathBuf%3E-for-PathBuf) implementation,
but may aid in type inference.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
use std::path::PathBuf;
let utf8_path_buf = Utf8PathBuf::from("foo.txt");
let std_path_buf = utf8_path_buf.into_std_path_buf();
assert_eq!(std_path_buf.to_str(), Some("foo.txt"));
// Convert back to a Utf8PathBuf.
let new_utf8_path_buf = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(std_path_buf).unwrap();
assert_eq!(new_utf8_path_buf, "foo.txt");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#268)#### pub fn [with_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.with_capacity)(capacity: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#268)

#### pub fn [with_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.with_capacity)(capacity: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html)

Creates a new [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html) with a given capacity used to create the internal

[. See](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)

`PathBuf`[defined on](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html#method.with_capacity)

`with_capacity`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)

`PathBuf`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::with_capacity(10);
let capacity = path.capacity();
// This push is done without reallocating
path.push(r"C:\");
assert_eq!(capacity, path.capacity());
```
Consumes and leaks the [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html), returning a mutable reference to the contents,

`&'a mut Utf8Path`.The caller has free choice over the returned lifetime, including ’static. Indeed, this function is ideally used for data that lives for the remainder of the program’s life, as dropping the returned reference will cause a memory leak.

It does not reallocate or shrink the [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html), so the leaked allocation may include
unused capacity that is not part of the returned slice. If you want to discard excess
capacity, call

[, and then](https://docs.rs/struct.PathBuf.html#method.into_boxed_path)

`into_boxed_path`[instead. However, keep in mind that trimming the capacity may result in a reallocation and copy.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html#method.leak)

`Box::leak`*Requires Rust 1.89 or newer.*

Extends `self` with `path`.

If `path` is absolute, it replaces the current path.

On Windows:

- if `path`has a root but no prefix (e.g.,`\windows`), it replaces everything except for the prefix (if any) of`self`.
- if `path`has a prefix but no root, it replaces`self`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

Pushing a relative path extends the existing path:

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::from("/tmp");
path.push("file.bk");
assert_eq!(path, Utf8PathBuf::from("/tmp/file.bk"));
```
Pushing an absolute path replaces the existing path:

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::from("/tmp");
path.push("/etc");
assert_eq!(path, Utf8PathBuf::from("/etc"));
```
Truncates `self` to [ self.parent](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.parent).

Returns `false` and does nothing if [ self.parent](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.parent) is

[. Otherwise, returns](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None``true`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};
let mut p = Utf8PathBuf::from("/spirited/away.rs");
p.pop();
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("/spirited"), p);
p.pop();
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("/"), p);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#854)#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html) is absolute, i.e., if it is independent of
the current directory.

-
On Unix, a path is absolute if it starts with the root, so `is_absolute`and`has_root`
-
On Windows, a path is absolute if it has a prefix and starts with the root: `C:\windows`is absolute, while`C:temp`and`\temp`are not.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("foo.txt").is_absolute());
```
Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html) has a root.

-
On Unix, a path has a root if it begins with `/`.
-
On Windows, a path has a root if it: - has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g., `\windows`
- has a prefix followed by a separator, e.g., `C:\windows`but not`C:windows`
- has any non-disk prefix, e.g., `\\server\share`

- has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g.,

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-20)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/etc/passwd").has_root());
```
Returns the [ Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html) without its final component, if there is one.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in a root or prefix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar");
let parent = path.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(parent, Utf8Path::new("/foo"));
let grand_parent = parent.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(grand_parent, Utf8Path::new("/"));
assert_eq!(grand_parent.parent(), None);
```

#### pub fn [ancestors](https://docs.rs#method.ancestors)(&self) -> [Utf8Ancestors](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/camino/struct.Utf8Ancestors.html)<'_>

Produces an iterator over [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html) and its ancestors.

The iterator will yield the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html) that is returned if the

[method is used zero or more times. That means, the iterator will yield](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.parent)

`parent``&self`, `&self.parent().unwrap()`,
`&self.parent().unwrap().parent().unwrap()` and so on. If the [method returns](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.parent)

`parent`[, the iterator will do likewise. The iterator will always yield at least one value, namely](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None``&self`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-22)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar").ancestors();
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar").ancestors();
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("..")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
```

If the path is a normal file, this is the file name. If it’s the path of a directory, this is the directory name.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in

`..`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-23)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;

assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("tmp/foo.txt").file_name());

assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/.//").file_name());
assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/..").file_name());
assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("/").file_name());

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300)#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/camino/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300)

#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/camino/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_>

Produces an iterator over the [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/camino/enum.Utf8Component.html)s of the path.

When parsing the path, there is a small amount of normalization:

-
Repeated separators are ignored, so `a/b`and`a//b`both have`a`and`b`as components.
-
Occurrences of `.`are normalized away, except if they are at the beginning of the path. For example,`a/./b`,`a/b/`,`a/b/.`and`a/b`all have`a`and`b`as components, but`./a/b`starts with an additional`CurDir`
-
A trailing slash is normalized away, `/a/b`and`/a/b/`are equivalent.

Note that no other normalization takes place; in particular, `a/c`
and `a/b/../c` are distinct, to account for the possibility that `b`
is a symbolic link (so its parent isn’t `a`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
let mut components = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").components();
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::RootDir));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("tmp")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), None)
```
Produces an iterator over the path’s components viewed as [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)
slices.

For more information about the particulars of how the path is separated
into components, see [ components](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.components).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut it = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").iter();
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string().as_str()));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("tmp"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("foo.txt"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), None)
```

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the destination file.

This is an alias to [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-37)Examples

```

```

Returns `true` if the path points at an existing entity.

Warning: this method may be error-prone, consider using [ try_exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.try_exists) instead!
It also has a risk of introducing time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

use camino::Utf8Path;

[Source](https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581)#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)>

#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)>

Returns `Ok(true)` if the path points at an existing entity.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `Ok(false)`.

As opposed to the [ exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html#method.exists) method, this one doesn’t silently ignore errors
unrelated to the path not existing. (E.g. it will return

[in case of permission denied on some of the parent directories.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)

`Err`Note that while this avoids some pitfalls of the `exists()` method, it still can not
prevent time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs. You should only use it in scenarios
where those bugs are not an issue.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-46)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(
    !Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt")
        .try_exists()
        .expect("Can't check existence of file does_not_exist.txt")
);
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/root/secret_file.txt").try_exists().is_err());
```

# Version in cargo_deny - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cargo-deny/0.19.9/cargo_deny/struct.Version.html

```
pub struct Version {
    pub major:
```
[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html),
    pub minor: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html),
    pub patch: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html),
    pub pre: [Prerelease](https://docs.rs/semver/1.0.28/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/semver/struct.Prerelease.html),
    pub build: [BuildMetadata](https://docs.rs/semver/1.0.28/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/semver/struct.BuildMetadata.html),
}## Expand description

**SemVer version** as defined by [https://semver.org](https://semver.org).

[§](https://docs.rs#syntax)Syntax

-
The major, minor, and patch numbers may be any integer 0 through u64::MAX. When representing a SemVer version as a string, each number is written as a base 10 integer. For example, `1.0.119`.
-
Leading zeros are forbidden in those positions. For example `1.01.00`is invalid as a SemVer version.
-
The pre-release identifier, if present, must conform to the syntax documented for `Prerelease`
-
The build metadata, if present, must conform to the syntax documented for `BuildMetadata`
-
Whitespace is not allowed anywhere in the version.

[§](https://docs.rs#total-ordering)Total ordering

Given any two SemVer versions, one is less than, greater than, or equal to the other. Versions may be compared against one another using Rust’s usual comparison operators.

-
The major, minor, and patch number are compared numerically from left to right, lexicographically ordered as a 3-tuple of integers. So for example version `1.5.0`is less than version`1.19.0`, despite the fact that “1.19.0” < “1.5.0” as ASCIIbetically compared strings and 1.19 < 1.5 as real numbers.
-
When major, minor, and patch are equal, a pre-release version is considered less than the ordinary release: version `1.0.0-alpha.1`is less than version`1.0.0`.
-
Two pre-releases of the same major, minor, patch are compared by lexicographic ordering of dot-separated components of the pre-release string. -
Identifiers consisting of only digits are compared numerically: `1.0.0-pre.8`is less than`1.0.0-pre.12`.
-
Identifiers that contain a letter or hyphen are compared in ASCII sort order: `1.0.0-pre12`is less than`1.0.0-pre8`.
-
Any numeric identifier is always less than any non-numeric identifier: `1.0.0-pre.1`is less than`1.0.0-pre.x`.

-

Example: `1.0.0-alpha` < `1.0.0-alpha.1` < `1.0.0-alpha.beta` < `1.0.0-beta` < `1.0.0-beta.2` < `1.0.0-beta.11` < `1.0.0-rc.1` < `1.0.0`

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.major)

`major: `[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.minor)

`minor: `[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.patch)

`patch: `[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.pre)

`pre: `[Prerelease](https://docs.rs/semver/1.0.28/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/semver/struct.Prerelease.html)[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.build)

`build: `[BuildMetadata](https://docs.rs/semver/1.0.28/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/semver/struct.BuildMetadata.html)## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Create `Version` with an empty pre-release and build metadata.

Equivalent to:

```
Version {
    major,
    minor,
    patch,
    pre: Prerelease::EMPTY,
    build: BuildMetadata::EMPTY,
}
```
Create `Version` by parsing from string representation.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Possible reasons for the parse to fail include:

-
`1.0`— too few numeric components. A SemVer version must have exactly three. If you are looking at something that has fewer than three numbers in it, it’s possible it is a`VersionReq`instead (with an implicit default`^`comparison operator).
-
`1.0.01`— a numeric component has a leading zero.
-
`1.0.unknown`— unexpected character in one of the components.
-
`1.0.0-`or`1.0.0+`— the pre-release or build metadata are indicated present but empty.
-
`1.0.0-alpha_123`— pre-release or build metadata have something outside the allowed characters, which are`0-9`,`A-Z`,`a-z`,`-`, and`.`(dot).
-
`23456789999999999999.0.0`— overflow of a u64.

[Source](https://docs.rs/semver/1.0.28/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/semver/lib.rs.html#466)

#### pub fn [cmp_precedence](https://docs.rs#method.cmp_precedence)(&self, other: &[Version](https://docs.rs/struct.Version.html)) -> [Ordering](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/enum.Ordering.html)

Compare the major, minor, patch, and pre-release value of two versions, disregarding build metadata. Versions that differ only in build metadata are considered equal. This comparison is what the SemVer spec refers to as “precedence”.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use semver::Version;
let mut versions = [
    "1.20.0+c144a98".parse::<Version>().unwrap(),
    "1.20.0".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.0.0".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.0.0-alpha".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.20.0+bc17664".parse().unwrap(),
];
// This is a stable sort, so it preserves the relative order of equal
// elements. The three 1.20.0 versions differ only in build metadata so
// they are not reordered relative to one another.
versions.sort_by(Version::cmp_precedence);
assert_eq!(versions, [
    "1.0.0-alpha".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.0.0".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.20.0+c144a98".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.20.0".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.20.0+bc17664".parse().unwrap(),
]);
// Totally order the versions, including comparing the build metadata.
versions.sort();
assert_eq!(versions, [
    "1.0.0-alpha".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.0.0".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.20.0".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.20.0+bc17664".parse().unwrap(),
    "1.20.0+c144a98".parse().unwrap(),
]);
```

# LintLevel in cargo_deny - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cargo-deny/0.19.9/cargo_deny/enum.LintLevel.html

```
pub enum LintLevel {
    Allow,
    Warn,
    Deny,
}
```
## Expand description

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Allow)

### Allow

A debug or info diagnostic *may* be emitted if the lint is violated

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Warn)

### Warn

A warning will be emitted if the lint is violated, but the command will succeed

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Deny)

### Deny

An error will be emitted if the lint is violated, and the command will fail with a non-zero exit code

# cargo_deny - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cargo-deny/latest/cargo_deny/

## Expand description

See the [book 📕](https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/) for in-depth documentation.

To run on CI as a GitHub Action, see [ cargo-deny-action](https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action).

*Please Note: This is a tool that we use (and like!) and it makes sense to us to release it as open source. However, we can’t take any responsibility for your use of the tool, if it will function correctly or fulfil your needs. No functionality in - or information provided by - cargo-deny constitutes legal advice.*

`cargo install --locked cargo-deny && cargo deny init && cargo deny check`[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

If you want to use `cargo-deny` without having `cargo` installed, build `cargo-deny` with the `standalone` feature. This can be useful in Docker Images.

```
cargo install --locked cargo-deny
# Or, if you're an Arch user
pacman -S cargo-deny
```
[§](https://docs.rs#initialize-your-project)[Initialize](https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/cli/init.html) your project

`cargo deny init``cargo deny check`The licenses check is used to verify that every crate you use has license terms you find acceptable.

`cargo deny check licenses`The bans check is used to deny (or allow) specific crates, as well as detect and handle multiple versions of the same crate.

`cargo deny check bans`The advisories check is used to detect issues for crates by looking in an advisory database.

`cargo deny check advisories`The sources check ensures crates only come from sources you trust.

`cargo deny check sources`[§](https://docs.rs#pre-commit-hook)Pre-commit hook

You can use `cargo-deny` with [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com). Add it to your local `.pre-commit-config.yaml` as follows:

```
- repo: https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny
  rev: 0.14.16 # choose your preferred tag
  hooks:
    - id: cargo-deny
      args: ["--all-features", "check"] # optionally modify the arguments for cargo-deny (default arguments shown here)
```

# cargo-deny 0.19.9 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cargo-deny/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please

# anyhow 1.0.103 - Docs.rs
